## **Life Story**

Judith Mae "Judy" Palmer was born February 9, 1939, the daughter of William Peter Palmer and Mary Jane Williams, and grew up in Cincinnati, one of three sisters, with Mary Ann and Penny beside her. ** \[FAMILY ACCOUNT\]** Her father's parents, Peter Palmer and Margaret Lorch, were Austro-Hungarian immigrants who crossed the Atlantic before the First World War.

At seventeen she ran off to Tennessee with Homer William Brewster Jr., and they married on April 18, 1956, in Fentress County, Tennessee. ** \[DOCUMENTED\]** Vicki, their eldest daughter, tells the story as her mother told it to her. Judy had taken a ride with Homer down to Tennessee, where her grandparents were visiting people, and Homer had lied and told her he was eighteen. When her family found out, they had a fit. Judy told Homer they had to get married because she couldn't go back, so they found an old man and paid him ten dollars to stand up and say he was her father, because they were underage and needed somebody to give consent, and they got married. When they came back, her grandpa and the woman who raised her made them marry again, properly this time; no record of that second wedding has been found, and no wedding pictures exist. They hadn't planned any of it. It just happened because of circumstances. ** \[FAMILY ACCOUNT\]**

They raised four children in the Hamilton and Preble County areas. That first wedding was not the last. Several of Judy's marriages were to Homer — they married and divorced several times. ** \[FAMILY ACCOUNT\]** Susan, who married into the family and watched it up close, remembers it plainly: the marrying and divorcing, over and over, and that he was very abusive. That is the family's telling, carried here as they tell it. ** \[FAMILY ACCOUNT\]**

She later married Larry Clark, and they had a son, Barry, who died before she did. Family memory holds that Barry had HIV/AIDS; no record confirms it. Garry holds the stories of Barry and his father. ** \[FAMILY ACCOUNT\]** Her later surname was Clark. ** \[DOCUMENTED\]**

After Homer left for good, Judy held the family together from a house in Hartwell, with a pool in the backyard where the grandchildren and cousins swam. And then there was Ralph, Judy's boyfriend of ten to fifteen years, as Amanda and the cousins who knew them both confirm, standing beside her in the family photographs of those later years. ** \[FAMILY ACCOUNT\]**

The grandchildren years belonged to Judy's house. Rick remembers it this way: his dad would pick them up from their apartment in Deer Park and bring them to Judy's more than anywhere else. She had a pet raccoon once, and Rick may even remember seeing it swim in the pool. Anytime the kids got in her car, she made them sit in car seats, even when they were too big for them. Cousin Ryan lived with Judy for a time. Rick remembers smearing something all over Ryan's room and toys, and Ryan hitting him in the head with a big red Cincinnati Reds baseball bat in Judy's front yard — on accident, Ryan says, but Rick is pretty sure that was the first time he was ever knocked out. ** \[FAMILY ACCOUNT\]**

Vicki’s and Ron’s children: Lindsey, Jeremy, Ryan, Amanda, Stefanie, and Randy. ** \[FAMILY ACCOUNT\]**

Her son Michael's name would one day travel further than any of theirs. In the summer of 2012 he robbed eleven banks in ten states, was caught in Roland, Oklahoma, pleaded guilty, and received 135 months in federal prison. The FBI called him the Bucket List Bandit. His release status is not confirmed. ** \[SUPPORTED\]**

She died June 7, 2006, ** \[DOCUMENTED\]** and was buried at Spring Grove Cemetery, Cincinnati. ** \[SUPPORTED\]** What held was Judy, who fought through a complex life to raise her children, the quiet engine of a family that kept going.
